one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-22 after the close (source #3), so the 10-31 close will include the reaction. Guidance was $15.8-16.8B revenue, $0.38 non-GAAP EPS, ~42% gross margin (source #1). Intel has beaten guidance seven quarters in a row, server CPUs are supply-constrained and estimates are rising (source #6, source #20, source #21), so a beat is likely. But the stock is up about 258% in a year, trades around 60-70x NTM EPS (source #3, source #6), and sold off about 9% from $127 to $116 in the week of 9-24 to 9-28 on rate fears, with the 10-year yield at its highest since 2007 (source #22). A beat may already be priced in, and any wobble on capex, the foundry loss rate (about $2B+ a quarter) or 14A customers could be punished. I see no edge in direction, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median about $119 (a slight downside tilt for rates and mean reversion) and a 1-month sigma of about 22% (76% annual vol / 3.5, kept flat rather than widened because the earnings move is already part of realized vol).

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on NTM EPS a year out ($2.50 x 35x = $88), a SOTP ($99) and EV/sales (7x 2027 revenue of $72B = $93). Weights are 0.40/0.35/0.25, giving about $93.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS as of Oct-2027 (Q4'27 + 3/4 of 2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS is $2.06 (source #6, source #21) and normalized 2028 is about $3 (source #3), so a blend is about $2.75. I cut it ~10% because the CPU-shortage pricing (10-15% server price hikes, source #20) may fade, and Northland expects datacenter spend to fall in CY27 (source #8).

AMD trades at about 40x forward and NVDA at about 25x (source #6). Northland called 38x on $3.20 'expensive' (source #8). Intel's 5-year median P/E is about 12x (source #13). 35x still prices growth and a foundry option but no longer a shortage-peak multiple.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Products (CCPG + DCAI) ~$22B 2027 op income, after 15% tax ~$18.7B x 25x = $467B; Foundry $120B; Mobileye/Altera stakes $9.4B; minus unallocated corporate costs $50B, net debt $5B and NCI $15.6B. That is about $525B / 5.30B shares = $99.

inputs_detail.derivation: About 14% growth on the Q2 run-rate, in line with consensus 2027 revenue growth of ~14% (source #21).
Same multiple source #5 uses for Intel Products, inside the 25-40x range of semi peers (source #6).

Net PP&E is $105.7B (source #1). Foundry loses about $2.1-2.5B a quarter with breakeven targeted for end-2027 and possibly slipping into 2028 (source #3); external revenue is only $293M a quarter (source #5). I give about 1.1x net PP&E for the strategic and government-backed value and the 18A yield progress (source #17) and 14A evaluations (source #18), well below source #5's ~$250B implied residual.
Q2 corporate unallocated was -$1.42B (source #1). I take ~$3B a year net of non-GAAP adjustments and capitalize it at about 17x after tax.

Q2 debt $50.5B less cash $12.9B + ST investments $16.9B (source #1) = $20.8B; less ~$19.7B offering net proceeds (source #2) = ~$1B; add ~$4B for H2 cash burn (Q2 adj. FCF -$8.4B, source #1, much of it the $14.3B partner distribution).
5,104M Q2 diluted (source #1) + 210.5M offering shares (source #2), ~5.285B per source #5; rounded to 5.30B to allow for greenshoe/escrow drift (143M escrowed DOC shares, source #4, not fully added).

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $72B x 7.0x = $504B EV; less net debt $5B and NCI $15.6B, plus stakes $9.4B, is about $492B / 5.30B = $93.

inputs_detail.derivation: source #4 puts the current multiple at about 10x sales, the $74 bear case at 5.9x and the $172 bull at 13.7x. I use 7x, leaning to the bear side because negative FCF and an unproven foundry argue against a full AI-semi multiple.

Q2 debt $50.5B less cash $12.9B + ST investments $16.9B (source #1) = $20.8B; less ~$19.7B offering net proceeds (source #2) = ~$1B; add ~$4B for H2 cash burn (Q2 adj. FCF -$8.4B, source #1, much of it the $14.3B partner distribution).
5,104M Q2 diluted (source #1) + 210.5M offering shares (source #2), ~5.285B per source #5; rounded to 5.30B to allow for greenshoe/escrow drift (143M escrowed DOC shares, source #4, not fully added).

bear.story: The CPU shortage eases and hyperscaler capex flattens in 2027 (Northland's call, source #8), so DCAI growth slows from +59% and server price increases reverse. No high-volume external 14A customer signs, and Intel signals a 14A pause (source #6). Foundry breakeven slips to 2028 (source #3) while FCF stays negative after the $20B raise (source #1, source #2). The multiple falls to about 6x sales and ~25x EPS (source #4, source #7). Price $60-75.

base.story: The turnaround continues: DCAI keeps growing, gross margin edges toward the mid-40s, 2027 EPS lands near $2.0-2.2 (source #21), and Apple/18A-P work progresses (source #19) without a blockbuster volume commitment. Earnings growth absorbs some de-rating from about 65x toward about 45x NTM. The stock ends roughly flat to slightly down, close to the street mean target of about $116 (source #6).

bull.story: A named high-volume 14A/18A-P customer is announced (Apple, Nvidia or a hyperscaler, source #18, source #19), the agentic-AI CPU shortage persists into 2027 (source #20), and 2028 EPS heads to $3+ (source #3, source #8). That matches source #4's $172 bull case at about 13.7x sales.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $70 (about 6x sales, ~42% below spot; source #4's bear case is $74 and source #5's is $70) the market would be pricing not just multiple compression but a fundamental break: the server-CPU upcycle rolling over and/or 14A losing its external customers, with foundry losses running at $2B+ a quarter and no breakeven path (source #3, source #6). It would also put the stock below the $95 offering and CEO purchase price by a wide margin (source #2, source #16). A fall to the $90s would be ordinary volatility given 76% realized vol and the $89 low in September.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Facts: Q2'26 revenue was $16.1B (+25%), non-GAAP EPS $0.42 and GAAP EPS -$2.16 (a $12.5B+ escrow mark-to-market loss). Adjusted FCF was -$8.4B, debt is $50.5B and foundry lost $2.1B on only $293M of external revenue (source #1, source #5). In August Intel raised about $20B in equity at $95 (source #2), which tells me the cash need is real even at peak sentiment. Credit is investment grade but weak (Baa2/BBB, Fitch negative outlook; source #9, source #10), with tech CDS widening in 2026 (source #12) and new long-dated notes at up to 6.2% (source #11). Valuation is the core of the bear case: about 63-69x NTM, 57x consensus 2027 EPS of $2.06, about 10x sales and roughly $635B of market cap (source #3, source #4, source #5, source #6). Comparisons to Cisco's 2000 peak multiple are in circulation (source #13). The street is mostly Hold, with a mean target of about $116, below spot (source #6), and Northland downgraded at a similar price in May, modelling a CY27 datacenter decline (source #8). Weighing this honestly: estimates rose about 35% in 90 days, server demand exceeds supply (source #20, source #21), 18A yields of about 80% are reported (source #17), eight major firms are evaluating 14A (source #18), Apple has a preliminary deal (source #19), and the CEO bought $10M at $95 with no meaningful insider selling (source #16). Short interest is only about 3% (source #15), the dismissed class action is a minor risk (source #14), and I found no accounting red flags beyond the escrow mark-to-market noise. My fundamental fair value is about $93 (P/E, SOTP and EV/sales), about 22% below spot. For the forecast I do not put the median at fair value. I set the 12-month median at about $108-110, roughly 10% below spot, as a compromise between my fair value and the market's momentum and evidence of rising estimates. The spread is a lognormal with sigma about 0.62 plus a 15% wide (sigma 1.0) tail component, a little below the 76% realized vol because vol tends to mean-revert, but fat-tailed for binary foundry and customer news. That gives P(>=120) of about 0.45 and P(<72) of about 0.26, consistent with the scenario weights (bear 30% at $65, base 45% at $110, bull 25% at $175; mean about $113). Limits: Seeking Alpha and Advisor Perspectives returned 403, I did not fetch X posts, and I found no relevant Polymarket or Kalshi market, so none is quoted.
